issue.title: Compilation errors with Clang and C++11 or C++14 (in func_trigonometric.inl)
issue.body:
I'm getting compilation errors when compiling with Clang using C++11 or C++14. With GCC and C++11/14 everything compiles fine. I'm compiling on Ubuntu 15.10.

Adding `std::` in front of the `asinh`, `acosh` and `atanh` on the lines which give the errors seems to fix this.

I assume the `#if GLM_HAS_CXX11_STL` isn't working correctly here?

``` cpp
    // asinh
#   if GLM_HAS_CXX11_STL
        this seems to be removed // by the preprocessor, even if I compile with C++11 or C++14
        using std::asinh;
#   else
        template <typename genType> 
        GLM_FUNC_QUALIFIER genType asinh(genType const & x)
        {
            GLM_STATIC_ASSERT(std::numeric_limits<genType>::is_iec559, "'asinh' only accept floating-point input");

            return (x < static_cast<genType>(0) ? static_cast<genType>(-1) : (x > static_cast<genType>(0) ? static_cast<genType>(1) : static_cast<genType>(0))) * log(std::abs(x) + sqrt(static_cast<genType>(1) + x * x));
        }
#   endif

    template <typename T, precision P, template <typename, precision> class vecType>
    GLM_FUNC_QUALIFIER vecType<T, P> asinh(vecType<T, P> const & v)
    {
        return detail::functor1<T, T, P, vecType>::call(asinh, v);  // <- error here, if I don't change `asinh` -> `std::asinh`
    }
```

body: And if it's of any use (the diffs must be huge by now), the version I was using previously (without any of these errors or warnings) was 93d09e0e.
And another note: I'm compiling with C++14, but I doubt the error and warnings would be any different with C++11. (BTW, C++14 will be the new default starting with GCC 6)

This issue is fixed in master branch. 

GLM requires anonymous struct for both swizzle operators and SIMD optimizations. If neither are used (GLM_SWIZZLE not defined before including GLM, no SIMD command line argument set to the compiler) then anonymous struct isn't used.

The fixes simply silent the warnings but the code check that anonymous struct is supported by the compilers. If it's not supported, then SIMD optimizations and swizzle operators are disabled.

Thanks for reporting,
Christophe

After some investigations I pushed a fix that might (tm) I just pushed do something about this bug.

Thanks!

I'm cloning GLM, but I'm using a slightly modified version, because I'm using GLM's headers as input for SWIG in order to generate Lua wrappers for it, to use it in our game engine. The modifications shouldn't change how GLM is compiled though, I'm just hiding parts of the code from SWIG.

I just did a fresh clone, and using _unmodified_ GLM source files, I created the smallest possible test file which gives the warning:

``` cpp
// main.cpp

}
```

issue.title: GLM can't handle -Wpedantic again (GLM 0.9.9.2)
issue.body:
similar to this issue #524 

Since 2016, GLM has been modified such that anonymous struct checks against GCC `-Wpedantic` cause warnings again.   This appears to be because [`glm/detail/type_vec2.hpp`](https://github.com/g-truc/glm/blob/master/glm/detail/type_vec2.hpp),  [`glm/detail/type_vec3.hpp`](https://github.com/g-truc/glm/blob/master/glm/detail/type_vec3.hpp) and [`glm/detail/type_vec4.hpp`](https://github.com/g-truc/glm/blob/master/glm/detail/type_vec4.hpp) have actually *removed* the fix seen [*already in use here* ](https://github.com/g-truc/glm/commit/2a3d241d78201ff9e8e9a34041686fbe670cb77e)

error example:

```
.../glm/detail/type_vec4.hpp:34:28: error: ISO C++ prohibits anonymous structs [-Werror=pedantic]
     struct { T s, t, p, q; };
                            ^
```

Last time the following lines were used to simply suppress compiler warnings at critical sites, like so:

```
#if GLM_COMPILER & GLM_COMPILER_GCC
#				pragma GCC diagnostic push
#				pragma GCC diagnostic ignored "-Wpedantic"
#			endif
#			if GLM_COMPILER & GLM_COMPILER_CLANG
#				pragma clang diagnostic push
#				pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wgnu-anonymous-struct"
#				pragma clang diagnostic ignored "-Wnested-anon-types"
#			endif

 ... // anonymous struct code

#			if GLM_COMPILER & GLM_COMPILER_CLANG
#				pragma clang diagnostic pop
#			endif
#			if GLM_COMPILER & GLM_COMPILER_GCC
#				pragma GCC diagnostic pop
#			endif

```

Is there a reason why this has since been ***removed*** as of the latest development branch (as far as I can tell)? There doesn't appear to be a way to simply mute anonymous struct warnings in GCC and pedantic is required for my code base. 

I'm able to make the changes locally with no pedantic errors, but I believe this issue has actually regressed into all places where it was previously needed (quaternion and vec1 need this as well?)
